summary: Candidate B closely follows the frozen contract, while Candidate A changes the established Add API’s behavior and bypasses it from Upload.
reasons: B adds the exact Upload signature, validates empty filenames and nil readers before encoding, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field "file", and delegates to FilesService.Add as required.
B preserves Add unchanged, maintaining its lower-level behavior for callers supplying custom multipart bodies.
B’s tests directly cover multipart field/name/content, retrying non-seekable streamed content, pre-request validation, and source-reader error propagation.

A unconditionally reads and buffers every Add body, which changes Add’s behavior, memory use, error timing, and reader semantics despite the contract requiring it to remain unchanged. Its changelog explicitly advertises this out-of-scope behavior change as a fix to Add itself instead of limiting replayability to Upload-produced bodies only via established mechanisms such as Add/request construction handling replayable readers (as B does by passing the helper-produced body). B's delegation is exactly contract fidelity; A introduces a private add path and has Upload bypass Add, duplicating routing structure and violating the requirement to route through the existing method so handling remains centralized. A also omits visible tests for empty filename, nil content, and source-reader errors.
risks_a: The new io.ReadAll in Add may unexpectedly consume large custom multipart bodies into memory and changes when reader errors occur.
Upload calls the private add helper instead of Add, allowing the two paths’ validation or behavior to diverge later.
Required validation and source-reader error cases are not visibly tested.
risks_b: The retry test validates multipart metadata only in the separate non-retry test; it checks retried content but not the retried field name and filename.
No changelog entry documents the new convenience API, though the contract does not require one.
